text: Sure. Evals is a way to systematically measure and improve an AI application, and it really doesn't have to be scary or unapproachable at all.
speaker: Hamel Husain
context: Lenny asks Hamel to explain what evals are for people who have never heard the term. Hamel provides a foundational definition, emphasizing that evals are not mysterious or complex but simply a systematic approach to measuring and improving AI applications through data analysis.
text_ko: 물론이에요. 에벌스(Evals)는 AI 애플리케이션(AI application)을 체계적으로 측정하고 개선하는 방법이에요. 전혀 무섭거나 접근하기 어려운 게 아니니 겁먹을 필요 없어요.
text_zh: 没错。Evals就是系统性地测评和改进AI应用的方法，其实真的没那么可怕，也不是什么高不可攀的东西。
text_es: Claro. Las evaluaciones (evals) son una forma de medir y mejorar sistemáticamente una aplicación de IA, y la verdad es que no tiene por qué dar miedo ni ser algo complicado.
key_sentence: Evals systematically measure and improve AI applications without being unapproachable.
original_text: Sure. Evals is a way to systematically measure and improve an AI application, and it really doesn't have to be scary or unapproachable at all. It really is, at its core, data analytics on your LLM application and a systematic way of looking at that data, and where necessary, creating metrics around things so you can measure what's happening, and then so you can iterate and do experiments and improve.

vocabulary.definition: In a methodical and organized manner, often involving a structured approach to tasks or processes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, systematically addressing problems or processes ensures consistency and efficiency, particularly in project management and quality assurance.
vocabulary.nuance: This term implies a thoroughness that may be lacking in more casual or ad-hoc approaches; it is best used when emphasizing a disciplined methodology.

vocabulary.definition: To assess the size, amount, or degree of something using standard units or criteria.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, measuring performance metrics, customer satisfaction, or project outcomes is crucial for informed decision-making and strategic planning.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'measure' can refer to quantitative assessments, it can also imply qualitative evaluations; context is important to convey the intended meaning.

vocabulary.definition: To make or become better, enhancing the quality or performance of a product, service, or process.
vocabulary.businessContext: Continuous improvement is a key principle in business, especially in areas like product development and customer service, where enhancing offerings can lead to competitive advantage.
vocabulary.nuance: This term suggests a proactive approach to development and growth; it is often used in contexts where change is necessary or desired.

text: When you're doing this open coding, a lot of teams get bogged down in having a committee do this. For a lot of situations, that's wholly unnecessary. You don't want to make this process so expensive that you can't do it.
speaker: Hamel Husain
context: Lenny asks about the concept of a 'benevolent dictator' in the evals process. Hamel explains that when doing open coding (manually reviewing and categorizing AI application errors), teams often get stuck trying to involve everyone in the decision-making process, which slows things down unnecessarily.
text_ko: 오픈 코딩(open coding)을 할 때 많은 팀이 이 작업을 위원회에 맡기느라 일이 지체되는 경우가 많아요. 대부분의 상황에서는 그럴 필요가 전혀 없어요. 이 과정을 너무 비용이 많이 들게 해서 아예 못 하게 만들면 안 돼요.
text_zh: 做开放式编码(open coding)的时候，很多团队容易陷入委员会式的讨论中，其实大部分情况下完全没必要这样。你不能让这个流程变得太重，重到最后根本做不下去。
text_es: Cuando están haciendo esta codificación abierta (open coding), muchos equipos se atascan queriendo que sea un comité quien lo haga. Para muchas situaciones, eso no tiene ningún sentido. No quieren hacer que el proceso sea tan costoso que después no lo puedan hacer.
key_sentence: You don't want to make this process so expensive that you can't do it.
original_text: When you're doing this open coding, a lot of teams get bogged down in having a committee do this. For a lot of situations, that's wholly unnecessary. You don't want to make this process so expensive that you can't do it. You can appoint one person whose taste that you trust. It should be the person with domain expertise. Oftentimes, it is the product manager.

vocabulary.definition: To become overwhelmed or hindered by excessive details or complications.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business or tech environments, teams may become bogged down in lengthy decision-making processes or bureaucratic procedures, which can delay project progress.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase often carries a negative connotation, suggesting inefficiency or frustration, and is typically used in contexts where speed and agility are desired.

vocabulary.definition: Completely lacking in necessity; not needed at all.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, identifying actions or processes as wholly unnecessary can help streamline operations and eliminate wasteful practices.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase emphasizes the total absence of need, often used to critique excessive measures or redundancies in processes.

vocabulary.definition: Costing a lot of money; high in price.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, the term expensive often refers to projects, products, or processes that require significant financial investment, which can impact budgeting and resource allocation.
vocabulary.nuance: While it primarily refers to cost, it can also imply that the value received does not justify the high price, making it a critical consideration in cost-benefit analyses.

vocabulary.definition: A series of actions or steps taken to achieve a particular end.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, a process often refers to structured workflows or methodologies that guide teams in completing tasks efficiently and effectively.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply both formal procedures and informal methods, and it is essential to distinguish between them when discussing improvements or optimizations.

text: Everyone that does this immediately gets addicted to it. When you're building an AI application, you just learn a lot and you're like, 'Hmm, this is not how I want it to work. Okay.' And so that's just an example.
speaker: Hamel Husain
context: Hamel is explaining the process of manually reviewing AI application traces (logs of user interactions) to identify errors. He's describing how product teams react when they start systematically looking at how their AI applications are actually performing in real conversations with users.
text_ko: 한번 해보면 다들 바로 빠져들어요. AI 애플리케이션(AI application)을 만들다 보면 배우는 게 엄청 많아서 '음, 이건 내가 원하던 대로 작동하지 않네. 알겠어요.' 하고 생각하게 돼요. 그러니까 그건 그냥 하나의 예일 뿐이에요.
text_zh: 每个人一接触这个就上瘾了。你在搭建AI应用的时候，会学到很多东西，然后就会想"嗯，这不是我想要的效果，好吧。"这就是个典型的例子。
text_es: Todos los que hacen esto se enganchan de inmediato. Cuando estás desarrollando una aplicación de IA, simplemente aprendes un montón y te quedas como "Mmm, esto no es como quiero que funcione. Ok." Y bueno, ese es solo un ejemplo.
key_sentence: Everyone gets addicted to it when building an AI application.

vocabulary.definition: The act of putting something into operation; in technology, it often refers to software designed to perform specific tasks for users.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, an application can refer to software solutions that address particular business needs, enhancing productivity and user engagement.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can also imply practical use, distinguishing it from theoretical concepts or ideas.

text: One common question that we get from people at this stage is, 'Okay, I understand what's going on.
speaker: Shreya Shankar
context: Shreya is explaining why humans need to do the initial error analysis rather than automating it with AI. She's responding to a common misconception that LLMs can automatically identify problems in AI application traces without human domain expertise and product context.
text_ko: 이 단계에서 사람들이 자주 하는 질문 중 하나가 ‘알겠어요, 무슨 일이 일어나고 있는지는 이해했어요’예요.
text_zh: 我们经常听到处在这个阶段的人问："好，我明白是怎么回事了。
text_es: Una pregunta muy típica que nos hacen en esta etapa es: "Vale, ya entiendo lo que está pasando.
key_sentence: Okay, I understand what's going on.
original_text: One common question that we get from people at this stage is, 'Okay, I understand what's going on. Can I ask an LLM to do this process for me?' And I loved Hamel's most recent example because what we usually find when we try to ask an LLM to do this error analysis is it just says the trace looks good because it doesn't have the context needed to understand whether something might be bad product smell or not.

text: The goal is not to do evals perfectly, it's to actionably improve your product.
speaker: Shreya Shankar
context: Shreya is giving advice to people who feel intimidated about starting the evals process. She's addressing the common concern that people need to execute evals flawlessly, emphasizing that the primary objective is product improvement rather than perfect execution of the evaluation methodology.
text_ko: 목표는 평가(evals)를 완벽하게 하는 게 아니라, 그 결과를 바탕으로 실제로 제품을 개선할 수 있게 만드는 거예요.
text_zh: 目标不是把评估做得完美无缺，而是要能实实在在地改进你的产品。
text_es: El objetivo no es hacer las evaluaciones perfectas, sino mejorar tu producto de manera práctica.
key_sentence: The goal is to actionably improve your product through evals.
original_text: The goal is not to do evals perfectly, it's to actionably improve your product. We guarantee you, no matter what you do, if you're doing parts of these process, you're going to find ways of actionable improvement, and then you're going to iterate on your own process from there.

vocabulary.definition: In a manner that allows for practical implementation or direct action.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, 'actionably' refers to insights or data that can be directly applied to improve processes, products, or strategies.
vocabulary.nuance: This term emphasizes the importance of not just having information, but ensuring it can lead to tangible outcomes.

vocabulary.definition: To make or become better; to enhance the quality or value of something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'improve' often refers to optimizing processes, increasing efficiency, or enhancing product features to meet customer needs.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'improve' generally has a positive connotation, it can imply that the current state is inadequate or lacking.

text: People have been burned by evals in the past. People have done evals badly, so then they didn't trust it anymore, and then they're like, 'Oh, I'm anti evals.' I 100% empathize with that, because you should be anti Likert scale LLM judge.
speaker: Shreya Shankar
context: Lenny asks about the controversy and debate around evals in the AI community. Shreya explains why some people are skeptical of evals, noting that many have had bad experiences with poorly implemented evaluation systems. A Likert scale LLM judge refers to using AI to score outputs on a 1-5 or 1-7 rating scale rather than binary pass/fail judgments.
text_ko: 사람들이 과거에 평가(evals) 때문에 피해를 본 적이 있어요. 평가를 엉망으로 해서 신뢰를 잃었고, 그래서 '난 평가 반대야'라고 하는 사람이 나온 거예요. 저도 그 마음을 100% 공감해요. 리커트 척도(Likert scale) 기반 LLM 판정(LLM judge)에는 반대하는 게 맞아요.
text_zh: 很多人以前在评估(evals)上吃过亏。有些人把评估搞砸了，结果就不再相信这套东西，然后就说"我就是反对评估"。我完全理解这种想法，因为你确实应该反对那种李克特量表LLM判断(Likert scale LLM judge)的方式。
text_es: La gente ha tenido malas experiencias con las evaluaciones antes. Han hecho evaluaciones muy mal, entonces ya no confían en ellas, y dicen "Ay no, yo estoy en contra de las evaluaciones." Entiendo perfectamente esa postura, porque deberías estar en contra de los jueces LLM con escala Likert (Likert scale LLM judge).
key_sentence: People have been burned by evals and may be anti Likert scale.

vocabulary.definition: To understand and share the feelings of another person, often by putting oneself in their position.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, empathizing with clients or employees can enhance relationships and improve communication, leading to better collaboration and trust.
vocabulary.nuance: While empathizing is generally positive, overemphasizing it can sometimes lead to emotional bias in decision-making.
